title: Applications of differentiation and kinematics
summary: Use first and second derivatives to find and classify stationary points and inflection points, solve optimisation problems, and analyse motion.

keyterms.definition: A point higher than all nearby points; f′ = 0 and f″ < 0 (or f′ changes from + to −).
A point lower than all nearby points; f′ = 0 and f″ > 0 (or f′ changes from − to +).
f″(x), the rate of change of the gradient; it shows concavity.
A point where the concavity changes, so f″ changes sign.
Concave up where f″(x) > 0 and concave down where f″(x) < 0.
Finding the maximum or minimum value of a quantity, often under a constraint.
s(t), position relative to a fixed origin; can be negative.
v = ds/dt; its magnitude is speed.
The total length of path, ∫|v(t)| dt; never negative.

questions.prompt: Find the x-coordinates of the stationary points of y = x³ − 3x.
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 3x² − 3 = 0 gives x² = 1. ±√3 are where y = 0.

questions.prompt: For y = x³ − 3x, the stationary point at x = 1 is…
options: a point of inflection, since y″ = 0
questions.explanation: y″ = 6x = 6 at x = 1, so the curve is concave up there.

questions.text: A point of inflection is where the ___ changes.
questions.explanation: f″ changes sign at an inflection point.

questions.statement: If f″(a) = 0, then x = a must be a point of inflection.
questions.explanation: y = x⁴ has f″(0) = 0 but a minimum at 0. Check that f″ changes sign.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has perimeter 20 cm. Find its maximum area.
questions.explanation: A = x(10 − x); A′ = 10 − 2x = 0 at x = 5, giving a 5 × 5 square.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = x³ − 6x², where is f concave up?

questions.text: At a local maximum, f′(x) = 0 and f″(x) ___ 0.
questions.explanation: Concave down at the top of a hill.

questions.statement: On a closed interval, the global maximum can occur at an endpoint.
questions.explanation: Always compare the stationary values with the values at the endpoints.

questions.prompt: Match each condition to its conclusion.

pairs.right: Point of inflection at x = a

questions.explanation: The second derivative test fails when f″(a) = 0; use a sign table then.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of an optimisation problem.
items: Define variables and write an expression for the quantity
Use the constraint to write it in one variable
Differentiate and set the derivative to 0
Check the nature and answer in context
questions.explanation: Always state the final answer with units.

questions.prompt: s = t³ − 6t². Find the velocity at t = 1.
questions.explanation: v = 3t² − 12t = 3 − 12 = −9. −5 is the displacement.

questions.prompt: For v = 3t² − 12t, when is the particle at rest (t > 0)?
questions.explanation: 3t(t − 4) = 0 gives t = 0 or 4.

questions.text: Acceleration is the derivative of ___ with respect to time.
questions.explanation: a = dv/dt.

questions.statement: Speed is the magnitude of velocity.
questions.explanation: Speed = |v|, which ignores direction.

questions.prompt: Which expression gives the distance travelled from t = a to t = b?
questions.explanation: The integral of v gives the change in displacement, which cancels when the particle turns back.

questions.prompt: For v = 3t² − 12t (t ≥ 0), when is the particle speeding up?
questions.explanation: a = 6t − 12. Speed increases when v and a have the same sign: both negative on (0, 2), both positive for t > 4.

questions.text: If s = 5t − t², the initial velocity is ___ m s⁻¹.

questions.statement: Displacement can be negative but distance travelled cannot.
questions.explanation: Displacement includes direction from the origin; distance is a total length.

questions.prompt: Match each expression to the quantity.
questions.explanation: Differentiate to go down the list; integrate to go up.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to find displacement from a known acceleration.
items: Use the initial velocity to find c
Integrate again to get s(t) and use the initial position
questions.explanation: Each integration introduces a constant that needs an initial condition.
